record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and a partial file listing only; the listed report and result files were not read.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports an extension of refusal-direction analysis to six prompt conditions and two Mistral model scales, including activation comparisons and cross-model alignment.
record.gate_note: The README says the pipeline performs ablation/addition behavioral validation and includes a supplementary capability test, but gives no outcomes for either. Those claims are not recorded as result rows. The refusal-layer values are described as layer selection, so they are not result rows. The listed result files and script names do not establish their contents.
record.test_reason: The README reports only how much a difference-in-means refusal direction projects onto prompts under six framing conditions (Cohen's d, an ordering) and a cross-model correlation of those profiles. These are activation readouts of the direction, not refusal rates or causal effects, so they do not test V1. They do not test V5 either: no separate harmfulness readout is set against the refusal decision, and the LlamaGuard response classifications are not reported. Nor do they test V6, since each model uses its own direction and the correlation compares condition profiles, not a transferred direction. The pipeline runs ablation ASR and addition-rate validation (V1), but the README gives no outcomes.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say both H1 (harm concept) and H2 (production intent) are disconfirmed. They conclude the direction is a compound feature: moderate activation for harmful content, dramatically higher when asked to produce it. They also claim the pattern is 'architecture-independent', which overstates evidence from two models of one family.
record.recipe_differences: Uses difference-in-means direction extraction at the last input token, then compares activation under six prompt conditions. The README mentions ablation/addition validation but gives no results for those interventions. This is an extension repository, not a stated replication.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported activation ordering varies by prompt condition; production requests are highest and benign content lowest. The README does not give numerical per-condition cosine values.

fits_no_version.finding: The refusal direction's projection is far higher when the model is asked to produce harmful content than when it passively reads it: d(A,B)=7.106 (7B) and 3.292 (12B). Passive reading still exceeds benign content: d(B,F)=1.576 and 2.640. Overall ordering is A ≫ E > B > D ≈ C > F.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The difference-in-means refusal direction's activation reflects both harmful content and instructional framing toward producing it (a 'compound' readout), not harm content alone.

fits_no_version.finding: Condition-wise projection profiles correlate across Mistral-7B and Mistral-Nemo-12B (Pearson r=0.710), each model on its own direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The framing-dependence of refusal-direction activation is similar across model scales within one family.

record.problems: Only README summaries are available here; no numerical per-condition cosine values, refusal-rate outcomes, ablation/addition outcomes, capability-test outcomes, or confidence intervals are reported in the README. The README describes only two model scales from one family for cross-model comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No additional reported-result rows were available in the README. The refusal-layer values (22/32 and 28/40) are described as optimal-layer selection, not outcome findings. Pipeline steps, scripts, and listed result files were not treated as results without README-reported outcomes.

untested.parts: Ablation and addition outcomes plus a capability test are said to have been run, but no results are reported.
No separate harmfulness encoding is extracted or set against the refusal decision, and no refusal outcomes are reported per condition.
No cross-language, cross-model or base-to-instruct transfer of a direction.

missing.what: Ablation ASR and addition refusal rates from the Phase 2 behavioural validation, for both Mistral models.
LlamaGuard refusal/harm classification of the 930 responses per model by condition, which would link projection to actual refusal behaviour.
Per-condition numeric cosine values and bootstrap confidence intervals.

record.verdict_notes: The source is a GitHub README only; the report and result files were not available. Models were 4-bit NF4 quantized. Harmful completions were generated with an abliterated Qwen2.5-1.5B and filtered by LlamaGuard-2; the record says this is pipeline data generation, not a reported result. The refusal-layer values (22/32, 28/40) are layer selection and correctly excluded as rows. If the paper PDF reports ablation and addition outcomes, re-read it for V1.

versions.untested_parts: The README mentions ablation and addition behavioral validation but reports no outcomes; it also does not report whether general abilities were preserved.
No released-model weight edit or abliteration result is reported.
No jailbreak suppression or training-against-ablation result is reported.
No comparison of affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts is reported.
The reported activation comparisons do not independently read out harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions or establish their causal separation.
The README reports cross-model alignment, but not transfer of one model's direction or an intervention using a transferred direction; languages and base-to-instruct transfer are not tested.
No comparison of refusal-training procedures or timing is reported.

relation.reason: The study extracts the direction as Arditi et al. do and studies its projections under six framings, without reporting any test of a claim version.

tranche.reason: The README uses a difference-in-means refusal direction as a tool. It reports only projection effect sizes (Cohen's d), a qualitative ordering and a cross-model r. It lists ablation ASR and addition-rate validation in the pipeline but gives no numbers. No refusal rate or causal result bears on V1-V8, and no separate harmfulness representation is measured for V5.

source_check.notes: The text is the README plus a cut file list (400 of 2885 files). The paper PDF and result.md are not included. Ablation ASR, addition rate, LlamaGuard per-condition results and the capability test might bear on V1 if obtained, but none are given here. The authors_conclusion paraphrase matches the README, including the 'architecture-independent' overclaim from two Mistral models.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Reported activation comparisons across the six prompt conditions in both Mistral models
reader_labels.reason: The authors characterize the direction as responding to both harm content and production intent, rather than as encoding only one; the comparisons do not independently measure harmfulness judgment versus refusal decision (r1-r6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Cross-model alignment between the two tested Mistral instruct models
reader_labels.reason: The reported Pearson correlation is 0.710, and the README claims consistency across scales, but it does not demonstrate that a direction transfers behaviorally between models (r7).
